prompt: How many ways can we place 8 books on a bookcase with 5 shelves if the books are (a) indistinguishable copies (b) all distinct? Note that the position of the books on the shelves does not matter. Note that all books may be placed on the same shelf.
judge_reasoning: Candidate 1 correctly computes (a) 495 via stars-and-bars and (b) 5^8 = 390625, fully matching the prompt’s “shelf positions don’t matter” condition. Candidate 2 and Candidate 4 both get (a) correct but produce incorrect values for (b) (34650 and 56, respectively). Candidate 3 gets (b) correct (5^8) but gives an incorrect (a) value (1296) with reasoning that conflicts with the indistinguishable-books setup, so it scores below Candidate 1 but above the other single-half-correct responses.
